label: cor:ftc_eval
title: Evaluation of integrals via antiderivatives
statement:
Let $f$ be continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ and let $F$ be any continuous antiderivative of $f$ on the interior. Then
    \[
      \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a).
    \]
proof: Set $G(u) = \int_a^u f(t)\,dt$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_is_antiderivative}, $G$ is an antiderivative of $f$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:antiderivatives_diff_constant}, $F - G$ is constant, so $F(b) - G(b) = F(a) - G(a)$. Since $G(a) = 0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_func_at_base}), we get $G(b) = F(b) - F(a)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:constant_diff_rearrangement}).
